title: Cost-Mosaic allocator: hybrid spot/on-demand routing with progressive model-variant fallbacks
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Design and implement a 'Cost-Mosaic' allocation policy in the routing layer that shards tenant spend into short windows and blends spot/on-demand GPU usage while automatically applying progressive model-variant fallbacks (precision reduction or distilled variant) when budget caps or preemption risk are high. Goal: keep P99 latency and quality SLOs for high-tier tenants while reducing excess on-demand spend and containing tenant monthly spend within configurable caps.
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy can accept per-tenant budget slices (windowed caps) and expose remaining budget to the routing decision engine.
Policy blends spot and on-demand pools using a configurable hedging factor and per-region spot-eviction probability for a target cost reduction of >=12% vs baseline for mixed workloads.

When preemption risk or remaining budget crosses thresholds, the router automatically selects the first available fallback in the variant chain (full -> quantized-8 -> int4/distilled) and respects latency SLOs.
A circuit-breaker stops fallbacks for tenants with explicit SLA holdouts (dedicated customers) and records a soft-failure event instead.
End-to-end tests that simulate spot evictions, budget exhaustion, and region outage show graceful degradation with <1% 5xx increase for canary tenants and fallback rate telemetry captured.
New dashboard presents per-tenant: budget remaining, fallback rate, cost per 1M tokens, spot-eviction incidents, and allocator decision trace links.
Policy rollout is gated by canary (5% of traffic) and a rollback path exists within 15 minutes via Console toggle.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Instrumentation - add short-window spend counters and per-tenant budget API; capture historical spot eviction rates by region/sku.
Phase 2: Variant Registry - extend model catalog with ordered fallback chains and precision profiles (latency/cost/quality metadata).
Phase 3: Router - implement Cost-Mosaic decision function in routing layer: inputs (budget_slice, eviction_prob, gpu_class_score, tenant_slo), outputs (region, instance_class, model_variant).
Phase 4: Scheduler integration - map router output to allocator hooks and pre-schedule hedged spot instances when allowed.
Phase 5: Observability - dashboards, alerts, and trace links; add decision logging for audit/QA (sampled to 1%).
Phase 6: Testing & Canary - chaos test spot evictions and region loss in staging; deploy to 5% canary and iterate.
Phase 7: Rollout - incremental ramp with traffic gating and runbook for manual override.
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% traffic (non-enterprise tenants) for 72 hours, monitor fallback rate and P99 latency.
Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks provided metrics stable.
Kill-switch: Console toggle to disable Cost-Mosaic routing globally; per-tenant override to force on-demand only.
Post-rollout review: 2-week retrospective and cost/quality comparison vs baseline.
